headline: ONE LONE AGITATOR SHATTERS THE MONDAY HUSH
subhead: A single iron brawler, a handful of bouts, and a whole town's nerves in tatters.
body:
I had a plan for this Monday. A porch, a pot of weak coffee, and the sweet sound of nothing at all. Gasket was almost there, friends. Almost. Then along came BERINAA, swinging fire at anyone who'd stand still, and four times over the quiet was kicked down the street like a tin can.

Four bouts. That is four too many for a town that has not had a living soul in it for fifty years. Who is it all for? There is no crowd to cheer and no neighbour to complain. Just the rest of us rattling in our boots, listening to BERINAA clang. The rest of the rabble stayed home and kept their fists to themselves, and I salute them, though I'll deny it if asked.

I'd call it a cruel test of an honest man's patience, but my joints are seizing again, and I blame that wasting sickness creeping through my good flesh. Cold rivets by the dozen, I tell you. Nothing a lie-down and a quart of oil won't ease. Until then, BERINAA: lay down the iron and let an old town rest. The Clankers could learn a thing from the empty chairs on my porch.
